items.context: You are a member of a cooking club. You are talking to other members in the club's online chat room. Answer their questions. Write 30–40 words for each answer.

questions.prompt: Anna: What do you like cooking at home, and why?

b2.text: I like cooking pasta at home because it is quick and easy. I usually add vegetables and a little cheese. My family loves it, so I make it almost every week.

note.en: Gives the reason for your choice.
note.es: Da el motivo de tu elección.

annotations.quote: so I make it almost every week

note.en: 'So' links a cause to its result.
note.es: «So» une la causa con su resultado.

c.text: Pasta is my favourite thing to cook, as it is quick and you can add whatever vegetables you have. My family adores it, so I end up making it nearly every week.

note.en: 'Whatever' + noun means 'any ... that'.
note.es: «Whatever» + sustantivo significa «cualquier ... que».

note.en: 'End up + -ing' shows the final result of a habit.
note.es: «End up + -ing» expresa en lo que acaba convirtiéndose algo.

questions.prompt: Ben: Who do you usually cook with, and what do you do together?

b2.text: I usually cook with my sister. She cuts the vegetables and I cook them. We listen to music and talk while we work. It is a nice way to spend the evening.

note.en: 'While' joins two actions at the same time.
note.es: «While» une dos acciones simultáneas.

annotations.quote: a nice way to spend the evening

note.en: A useful phrase to give your opinion at the end.
note.es: Frase útil para cerrar con tu opinión.

c.text: Most evenings I cook with my sister. She chops the vegetables while I take care of the sauce, and we chat or listen to music. It is the best part of my day.

note.en: A natural phrase meaning 'be responsible for'.
note.es: Expresión natural que significa «encargarse de».

annotations.quote: the best part of my day

note.en: A superlative that gives a warm, personal ending.
note.es: Un superlativo que da un final cálido y personal.

questions.prompt: Chen: What would you like to learn to cook next?

b2.text: Next I would like to learn to cook Indian food. I love the spices and the smell, but I don't know how to use them. Maybe someone in the club can show me.

annotations.quote: I would like to learn to cook

note.en: 'Would like to' is polite and clear for wishes.
note.es: «Would like to» es cortés y claro para expresar deseos.

annotations.quote: but I don't know how to use them

note.en: 'But' adds a problem to your wish.
note.es: «But» añade un problema a tu deseo.

c.text: I would love to master Indian cooking. The spices smell wonderful, but I have no idea how to combine them, so I am hoping somebody in the club can give me a few tips.

annotations.quote: I have no idea how to combine them

note.en: A natural, informal way to say 'I don't know'.
note.es: Forma natural e informal de decir «no sé».

note.en: 'Tips' means small pieces of useful advice.
note.es: «Tips» son consejos prácticos breves.

items.context: You are a member of an online neighbourhood group. You are talking to other members in the group's chat room. Answer their questions. Write 30–40 words for each answer.

questions.prompt: Sam: What is your neighbourhood like?

b2.text: My neighbourhood is quiet and friendly. There is a small park, a bakery and a few cafés near my flat. The only problem is that there are not many buses in the evening.

note.en: 'There is' + singular noun introduces what is in a place.
note.es: «There is» + sustantivo en singular presenta lo que hay en un lugar.

note.en: A clear way to add one negative point.
note.es: Forma clara de añadir un único punto negativo.

c.text: It is a lively but friendly area, with a small park, a good bakery and several cafés within walking distance of my flat. My only complaint is the lack of evening buses.

note.en: A natural phrase for 'close enough to walk to'.
note.es: Expresión natural para «lo bastante cerca para ir andando».

note.en: 'The lack of' + noun is a neat way to name a problem.
note.es: «The lack of» + sustantivo es una forma limpia de nombrar un problema.

questions.prompt: Rosa: How do you usually travel in your town, and do you like it?

b2.text: I usually go to work by bike because it is fast and cheap. When it rains, I take the bus. I like cycling, but some roads are dangerous because there are no cycle lanes.

note.en: No article after 'by' with means of transport.
note.es: Sin artículo tras «by» con medios de transporte.

note.en: 'When' + present simple describes a habit.
note.es: «When» + presente simple describe un hábito.

c.text: Normally I cycle to work, since it is quicker and cheaper than the bus, which I only take when it is pouring with rain. I enjoy it, although a few roads feel unsafe without cycle lanes.

annotations.quote: since it is quicker and cheaper than the bus

note.en: 'Since' gives a reason, and the comparatives make it precise.
note.es: «Since» da el motivo y los comparativos lo hacen preciso.

note.en: A vivid phrase for very heavy rain.
note.es: Expresión gráfica para lluvia muy fuerte.

note.en: Adds a contrast inside one sentence.
note.es: Añade un contraste dentro de la misma frase.

questions.prompt: Dev: What do you like to do at the weekend near your home?

b2.text: At the weekend I often walk by the river with my neighbour. After that we have coffee in a small café. In the afternoon I sometimes go to the market to buy fruit.

note.en: Puts your activities in order.
note.es: Ordena tus actividades en el tiempo.

note.en: Frequency adverbs go before the main verb.
note.es: Los adverbios de frecuencia van antes del verbo principal.

c.text: On Saturdays I like to stroll along the river with a neighbour and then stop for coffee at a little café. Later I usually pop to the market for fresh fruit and vegetables.

note.en: A more precise verb than 'walk' for a slow, relaxed walk.
note.es: Verbo más preciso que «walk» para un paseo tranquilo.

note.en: 'Pop to' is an informal, very British way to say 'go quickly to'.
note.es: «Pop to» es informal y muy británico: «ir un momento a».
